subject: maths
verifiedAgainst: NCERT textbook listing (ncert.nic.in/textbook.php) + table of contents in the book prelims PDF

topics.title: Numbers in thousands and beyond
outcomes: Learner can read, write and compare 5- and 6-digit numbers using place value and the Indian system of commas
misconceptions: Thinks the comma position is decorative and can go anywhere
Reads 10,500 as one thousand five hundred
hooks: Distances on the highway: Delhi to Kanyakumari

topics.title: Estimating large numbers
outcomes: Learner can round large numbers sensibly for estimates in travel contexts
misconceptions: Believes rounding changes the actual distance
hooks: About how far is your nani’s village?

topics.title: Fractions on the number line
outcomes: Learner can place fractions on a number line between 0 and 1 and beyond
misconceptions: Thinks fractions are not numbers and cannot go on the number line
hooks: How far along the road is the chai stall: halfway, one-third?

topics.title: Comparing fractions
outcomes: Learner can compare fractions with the same numerator or denominator and explain using pictures
misconceptions: Believes 1/8 > 1/4 because 8 > 4
hooks: Would you rather have 1/4 or 1/8 of a pizza?

topics.title: Equivalent fractions
outcomes: Learner can show that two fractions are equal using paper folding and grids
misconceptions: Thinks 2/4 is more than 1/2 because there are more pieces
hooks: Fold a chapati into halves then quarters

topics.title: Angles as amount of turning
outcomes: Learner can describe turns as quarter, half, three-quarter and full turns, clockwise and anticlockwise
misconceptions: Thinks an angle is the length of the lines, not the amount of turn
hooks: Turning the steering of an auto; a clock hand moving from 12 to 3

topics.title: Right, acute and obtuse angles
outcomes: Learner can compare angles with a right angle and classify them
misconceptions: Believes an angle that opens to the left is different from the same angle opening right
hooks: Angles made by scissors and a door opening

topics.title: Adding and subtracting large numbers
outcomes: Learner can add and subtract 5-digit numbers with regrouping in travel problems
misconceptions: Loses track of regrouping across zeros (10000 - 2345)
hooks: Kilometres covered on a family road trip

topics.title: Checking reasonableness
outcomes: Learner can use estimation and inverse operations to check answers
misconceptions: Thinks if the calculation steps are followed the answer must be right
hooks: Does your total distance make sense on the map?

topics.title: Kilometres, metres and centimetres
outcomes: Learner can convert between km, m and cm and choose suitable units
misconceptions: Believes 1 km = 100 m
hooks: How far is school in km and in m?

topics.title: Comparing distances
outcomes: Learner can compare and order distances given in mixed units
misconceptions: Compares numbers without matching the units (2 km < 500 m)
hooks: Distances between metro stations

topics.title: Multiplying larger numbers
outcomes: Learner can multiply 2- and 3-digit numbers by 2-digit numbers using place value and area models
misconceptions: Forgets the zero when multiplying by the tens digit (shift error)
hooks: Litres of milk collected at the Amul dairy each day

topics.title: Multiplication patterns and estimation
outcomes: Learner can use patterns like × 10, × 100 and doubling to multiply mentally
misconceptions: Thinks multiplying always makes a number bigger
hooks: Cost of 25 kg of fodder at ₹40/kg

topics.title: Triangles and polygons
outcomes: Learner can identify and describe triangles and polygons by sides and angles
misconceptions: Thinks a triangle with no horizontal base is not a triangle
hooks: Triangle patterns in jaali work

topics.title: Growing shape patterns
outcomes: Learner can continue shape patterns and predict the next term using a rule
misconceptions: Predicts the next term by guessing instead of looking for the change
hooks: Matchstick patterns of houses

topics.title: Converting kg and g
outcomes: Learner can convert between kg and g and solve problems with mixed units
misconceptions: Writes 2 kg 50 g as 2.50 kg
hooks: Parcel weights at the post office

topics.title: Converting l and ml
outcomes: Learner can convert between l and ml and compare capacities
misconceptions: Thinks 1 l 250 ml = 1250 l
hooks: How many 250 ml glasses of lassi in 2 l?

topics.title: Dividing larger numbers
outcomes: Learner can divide 3- and 4-digit numbers by 1- and 2-digit numbers and interpret remainders
misconceptions: Ignores the remainder or writes it as a decimal digit
hooks: Packing coconuts in sacks of 25 in Kerala

topics.title: Making sense of remainders
outcomes: Learner can decide whether to round up, down or keep the remainder in a real situation
misconceptions: Always drops the remainder even when it means someone is left out
hooks: How many autos for 23 students if 4 fit in each?

topics.title: Turn symmetry
outcomes: Learner can identify designs that look the same after a part turn
misconceptions: Thinks only shapes with a mirror line are symmetrical
hooks: A fan, a chakra, a flower rangoli

topics.title: Making symmetrical designs
outcomes: Learner can create designs with mirror and turn symmetry by folding, cutting or using dot grids
misconceptions: Thinks a design with turn symmetry must also have a mirror line
hooks: Cut-paper toran and kolam designs

topics.title: Area by counting squares
outcomes: Learner can find the area of shapes by counting unit squares and half squares
misconceptions: Confuses area with perimeter
Thinks shapes with the same perimeter have the same area
hooks: Patches on dadi’s quilt (kantha/godhadi)

topics.title: Perimeter of rectangles
outcomes: Learner can find the perimeter of rectangles and squares and relate it to the boundary
misconceptions: Adds just length and breadth once for the perimeter
hooks: Lace border needed for the quilt

topics.title: Same area, different shapes
outcomes: Learner can make different rectangles with the same area and compare their perimeters
misconceptions: Believes a longer rectangle always has more area
hooks: Arrange 12 tiles in different rectangles

topics.title: Seconds, minutes and hours
outcomes: Learner can measure short durations in seconds and convert between seconds, minutes and hours
misconceptions: Converts 1.5 hours as 1 hour 50 minutes
hooks: Timing a 100 m race on sports day

topics.title: Comparing timings
outcomes: Learner can compare and order times taken and find differences
misconceptions: Thinks a bigger time means a faster runner
hooks: Who won: 15.2 s or 14.8 s?

topics.title: Multiples and common multiples
outcomes: Learner can list multiples of a number and find common multiples
misconceptions: Confuses factors with multiples
hooks: A frog jumps 3, a rabbit jumps 4: where do they both land?

topics.title: Factors
outcomes: Learner can find all factors of a number by pairing
misconceptions: Thinks 1 and the number itself are not factors
hooks: Arrange 24 chairs in equal rows

topics.title: Directions and routes
outcomes: Learner can give and follow directions using north, south, east, west and landmarks
misconceptions: Believes north is always "up" in real life, not just on maps
hooks: Guide a friend from the bus stand to your house

topics.title: Reading distances on a map
outcomes: Learner can use a simple scale to find distances on a map
misconceptions: Measures map length and reports it as the real distance
hooks: School map: 1 cm stands for 10 m

topics.title: Pictographs with a scale
outcomes: Learner can draw and read pictographs where one symbol stands for many
misconceptions: Counts half-symbols as whole symbols
hooks: Hours of screen time per day in the class

topics.title: Bar graphs
outcomes: Learner can draw and read bar graphs and use them to answer questions
misconceptions: Starts the scale at a number other than 0 without noticing it changes comparisons
hooks: Monthly rainfall in Cherrapunji vs Jaisalmer
